name: John Konrads
milestone_by_age_26: Set multiple freestyle world records in January 1958 at age 15, becoming the best freestyle swimmer in the world; won 3 gold medals at the 1958 British Empire and Commonwealth Games at age 16.
early_history_summary: Born in Riga, Latvia during WWII, Konrads fled with his family to Germany in 1944 where he contracted polio in a refugee camp. The family migrated to Australia in 1949. His father taught the children to swim as therapy for John's polio. Under coach Don Talbot at Bankstown Swimming Pool, John and his sister Ilsa became the celebrated 'Konrads Kids', setting dozens of world records as teenagers. Between January 1958 and February 1960, the siblings established 37 world records.
family_context_summary: Born in Riga, Latvia during WWII; family fled to Germany in 1944 as refugees. John contracted polio in a refugee camp near Stuttgart. Family migrated to Australia in 1949 and lived in a refugee camp at Uranquinty, NSW, before settling in Sydney. Father taught children to swim.

evidence_summary: Konrads was a Latvian refugee who contracted polio in a German refugee camp before migrating to Australia at 7. His father taught him to swim as therapy, and coach Don Talbot transformed him and his sister Ilsa into world-record holders. The sibling training partnership was exceptional — both set world records simultaneously as the 'Konrads Kids'. Australia was the global frontier of swimming in the 1950s, and Talbot's strenuous training program (before and after school) provided the concentration and reps needed. By 15, Konrads held every freestyle world record from 200m to 1500m. His adversity (refugee, polio) was severe but catalyzed his swimming career through therapeutic origins.
